To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the teachers' appropriation of the problem was intense and mediated by their practice and that the argumentative strategies, mainly those of illustration and authority, were used to reinforce the collective knowledge construction.

the teachers' appropriation of the problem was expressed through hybrid and radical utterances and the argumentative strategies of real case and of ideas from the papers were used to reinforce the collaborative knowledge construction.
the teachers' appropriation of meaning of problem situations and of the research papers was mediated by their practice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interanimation of voices and with argumentation as strategies for the collaborative knowledge building among teachers in a CSCL environment.

the analysis of the discourse in an on-line discussion group in a constructivist learning environment, with the purpose of understanding the social construction of knowledge in the professional context.
the analysis of the inter-animation of voices in the context of collaborative knowledge building of teachers in an on-line course.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the analysis of the argumentation and the appropriation of meaning of utterances in an asynchronous discussion can help to identify the social construction of professional and scientific knowledge among teachers in an on-line collaborative learning environment.

this paper has contributed to the literature on CSCL by providing an in-depth analysis of the social construction of knowledge in the context of on-line discussion groups, and that this analysis has been carried out in the specific case of a group of in-service teachers, who are a particular category of learners, as they already have their own professional knowledge.
the teachers involved in this research used the on-line discussion as a tool for knowledge building, in which they appropriated the problem and the solutions proposed by their colleagues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of discourse analysis and argumentation analysis in CSCL research is a powerful tool for understanding how teachers learn in collaborative environments.

the teachers' professional knowledge was constructed by means of the interanimation of their voices and of the arguments, and that the argumentative strategies used in the discussion were more directed to reinforce the collaborative construction of the knowledge than to increase the participation of the participants.
the analysis of the argumentation strategies in CSCL can be used to identify the appropriation of knowledge by teachers, as well as the appropriation of the problem by them.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the analysis of argumentative strategies and the analysis of utterances can be used to identify how the participants in an on-line discussion group appropriate the ideas of their peers and the readings.

discourse analysis is a powerful tool for investigating how participants in a discussion group appropriate and use ideas from readings and how they use argumentative strategies to construct knowledge collaboratively.
discourse and argumentative strategies are powerful instruments for understanding the processes of collaborative construction of knowledge in the context of on-line discussion forums.
